rules.title: Privileged scheduled task runs a program that can be overwritten
rules.subject: {$parent.path}{$parent.name} -> {image_path}
rules.why: The task runs this program as SYSTEM, a service account, or with highest privileges. Anyone who can overwrite the program gets those rights the next time the task fires.
rules.fix: Restrict the program's ACL so only SYSTEM and Administrators can write it, or point the task at a copy in a protected folder (Program Files, System32). schtasks /query /tn "<task>" /v shows its triggers.

rules.title: Privileged scheduled task's program folder lets non-admins add files
rules.subject: {$parent.path}{$parent.name} -> {image_path}
rules.why: Windows looks in a program's own folder first when it loads a DLL. A DLL planted here under the name of one the program loads runs with the task's privileges.
rules.fix: Remove 'create files / write data' rights for non-admin accounts on the folder, or move the program into a protected folder and update the task.

rules.title: Privileged scheduled task runs a missing program that non-admins can create
rules.subject: {$parent.path}{$parent.name} -> {image_path}
rules.why: The task starts a program that no longer exists, in a place where non-admins can create it. Whoever puts a program there gets it run as SYSTEM, a service account, or with highest privileges the next time the task fires.
rules.fix: If the software is gone, delete the task (Task Scheduler, or schtasks /delete /tn "<task>" from an elevated prompt). Otherwise reinstall the program into a protected folder.

rules.title: Disabled privileged task would run a program non-admins can replace
rules.subject: {$parent.path}{$parent.name} -> {image_path}
rules.why: Not exploitable while the task stays disabled. If anything re-enables it (an update, a repair install, an admin), non-admins can supply the program it runs with high privileges.
rules.fix: Delete the task if nothing needs it (Task Scheduler, or schtasks /delete /tn "<task>" from an elevated prompt). Disabled tasks left behind by uninstalled software are safe to remove.
